title: Ensure 'Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation to 'Disabled'
reason: If this policy setting is enabled, a user with local access could use the well-known Administrator's SID to learn the real name of the built-in Administrator account, even if it has been renamed. That person could then use the account name to initiate a password guessing attack.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts to 'Enabled'
reason: An unauthorized user could anonymously list account names and use the information to attempt to guess passwords or perform social engineering attacks.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares to 'Enabled'
reason: An unauthorized user could anonymously list account names and shared resources and use the information to attempt to guess passwords or perform social engineering attacks.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication to 'Enabled'
reason: Passwords that are cached can be accessed by the user when logged on to the computer. A problem can arise if the user unknowingly executes hostile code that reads the passwords and forwards them to another, unauthorized user.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users to 'Disabled'
reason: An unauthorized user could anonymously list account names and shared resources and use the information to attempt to guess passwords, perform social engineering attacks, or launch DoS attacks.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Named Pipes that can be accessed anonymously' is configured
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Named Pipes that can be accessed anonymously to None or BROWSER
reason: Limiting named pipes that can be accessed anonymously will reduce the attack surface of the system.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths' is configured
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths
reason: The registry is a database that contains computer configuration information, and much of the information is sensitive. A threat actor could use this information to facilitate unauthorized activities.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths and sub-paths' is configured
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Remotely accessible registry paths and sub-paths
reason: The registry contains sensitive computer configuration information that could be used by a threat actor to facilitate unauthorized activities.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares to 'Enabled'
reason: Null sessions are a weakness that can be exploited through shares (including the default shares) on computers in your environment.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM' is set to 'Administrators: Remote Access: Allow'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Restrict clients allowed to make remote calls to SAM to 'Administrators: Remote Access: Allow'
reason: To ensure that an unauthorized user cannot anonymously list local account names or groups and use the information to attempt to guess passwords or perform social engineering attacks.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Shares that can be accessed anonymously' is set to 'None'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Shares that can be accessed anonymously to 'None'
reason: It is very dangerous to allow any values in this setting. Any shares that are listed can be accessed by any network user, which could lead to the exposure or corruption of sensitive data.

title: Ensure 'Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts' is set to 'Classic - local users authenticate as themselves'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts to 'Classic'
reason: With the Guest only model, any user who can authenticate to your computer over the network does so with guest privileges, which means that they will not have write access to shared resources on that computer. With the Classic model, local accounts should be password protected to maintain security.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM to 'Enabled'
reason: When connecting to computers running versions of Windows earlier than Windows Vista or Windows Server 2008, services running as Local System and using SPNEGO that revert to NTLM use the computer identity. This ensures both signing and encryption is supported.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback to 'Disabled'
reason: NULL sessions are less secure because by definition they are unauthenticated.

title: Ensure 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities to 'Disabled'
reason: The PKU2U protocol is a peer-to-peer authentication protocol - authentication should be managed centrally in most managed networks.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos' is set to 'AES128_HMAC_SHA1, AES256_HMAC_SHA1, Future encryption types'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos
reason: The strength of each encryption algorithm varies from one to the next, choosing stronger algorithms will reduce the risk of compromise however doing so may cause issues when the computer attempts to authenticate with systems that do not support them.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change to 'Enabled'
reason: The LM hash is relatively weak and prone to attack compared to the cryptographically stronger Microsoft Windows NT hash. The SAM file can be targeted by threat actors who seek access to username and password hashes.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire to 'Enabled'
reason: If this setting is disabled, a user could remain connected to the computer outside of their allotted logon hours.

title: Ensure 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' is set to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: LAN Manager authentication level to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM'
reason: LM responses - the weakest form of authentication response - were sent over the network, and it was potentially possible for threat actors to sniff that traffic to more easily reproduce the user's password. A more secure authentication protocol can be forced by using NTLMv2.

title: Ensure 'Network security: LDAP client signing requirements' is set to 'Negotiate signing' or higher
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: LDAP client signing requirements to 'Negotiate signing' or 'Require signing'
reason: Unsigned network traffic is susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks in which an intruder captures the packets between the client and server, modifies them, and then forwards them to the server.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients' is set to 'Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients
reason: Enable both options for this policy setting to help protect network traffic that uses the NTLM Security Support Provider from being exposed or tampered with by a threat actor who has gained access to the same network.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers' is set to 'Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers
reason: Enable all of the options for this policy setting to help protect network traffic that uses the NTLM Security Support Provider from being exposed or tampered with by a threat actor who has gained access to the same network.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic' is set to 'Enable auditing for all accounts'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Restrict NTLM: Audit Incoming NTLM Traffic
reason: Auditing and monitoring NTLM traffic can assist in identifying systems using this outdated authentication protocol, so they can be remediated to using a more secure protocol, such as Kerberos.

title: Ensure 'Network security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers' is set to 'Audit all' or higher
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Restrict NTLM: Outgoing NTLM traffic to remote servers
reason: Auditing and monitoring NTLM traffic can assist in identifying systems using this outdated authentication protocol, so they can be remediated to using a more secure protocol, such as Kerberos.

title: Ensure 'Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on' is set to 'Disabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on to 'Disabled'
reason: Users who can access the console locally could shut down the computer. Threat actors could also walk to the local console and restart the server, which would cause a temporary denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

title: Ensure 'System objects: Require case insensitivity for non-Windows subsystems' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\System objects: Require case insensitivity for non-Windows subsystems to 'Enabled'
reason: Because Windows is case-insensitive but the POSIX subsystem will support case sensitivity, failure to enable this policy setting would make it possible for a user of that subsystem to create a file with the same name as another file but with a different mix of upper and lower case letters.

title: Ensure 'System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g. Symbolic Links)' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g. Symbolic Links) to 'Enabled'
reason: This setting determines the strength of the default DACL for objects. Windows maintains a global list of shared computer resources so that objects can be located and shared among processes.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account to 'Enabled'
reason: One of the risks that the User Account Control feature introduced with Windows Vista is trying to mitigate is that of malicious software running under elevated credentials without the user or administrator being aware of its activity.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is set to 'Prompt for consent on the secure desktop' or higher
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode
reason: This setting raises awareness to the administrator of elevated privilege operations and permits the administrator to prevent a malicious program from elevating its privilege when the program attempts to do so.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users' is set to 'Automatically deny elevation requests'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users to 'Automatically deny elevation requests'
reason: This setting raises awareness to the user that a program requires the use of elevated privilege operations and requires that the user be able to supply administrative credentials in order for the program to run.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation to 'Enabled'
reason: Some malicious software will attempt to install itself after being given permission to run. For example, malicious software with a trusted application shell.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations to 'Enabled'
reason: UIAccess Integrity allows an application to bypass User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) restrictions when an application is elevated in privilege from a standard user to an administrator.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode to 'Enabled'
reason: This is the setting that turns on or off UAC. If this setting is disabled, UAC will not be used and any security benefits and risk mitigations that are dependent on UAC will not be present on the system.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation to 'Enabled'
reason: Standard elevation prompt dialog boxes can be spoofed, which may cause users to disclose their passwords to malicious software. The secure desktop presents a very distinct appearance when prompting for elevation.

title: Ensure 'User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations' is set to 'Enabled'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations to 'Enabled'
reason: This setting reduces vulnerabilities by ensuring that legacy applications only write data to permitted locations.
